verses.text: By those [angels] who extract with violence[1]
And [by] those who remove with ease[2]
And [by] those who glide [as if] swimming[3]
And those who race each other in a race[4]
And those who arrange [each] matter,[5]
On the Day the blast [of the Horn] will convulse [creation],
There will follow it the subsequent [one].
Hearts,[6] that Day, will tremble,
Their eyes[7] humbled.
They are [presently] saying, "Will we indeed be returned to [our] former state [of life]?
Even if we should be decayed bones?"[8]
They say, "That, then, would be a losing return."[9]
Indeed, it will be but one shout,
And suddenly they will be [alert] upon the earth's surface.
Has there reached you the story of Moses? -
When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Ṭuwā,
"Go to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed.
And say to him, 'Would you [be willing to] purify yourself
And let me guide you to your Lord so you would fear [Him]?'"
And he showed him the greatest sign,[10]
But he [i.e., Pharaoh] denied and disobeyed.
Then he turned his back, striving [i.e., plotting].[11]
And he gathered [his people] and called out.
And said, "I am your most exalted lord."
So Allāh seized him in exemplary punishment for the last and the first [transgression].[12].
Indeed in that is a lesson [i.e., warning] for whoever would fear [Allāh].
Are you a more difficult creation or is the heaven? He [i.e., Allāh] constructed it.
He raised its ceiling and proportioned it.
And He darkened its night and extracted its brightness.[13]
And after that He spread the earth.
He extracted from it its water and its pasture,
And the mountains He set firmly
As enjoyment [i.e., provision] for you and your grazing livestock.
But when there comes the greatest Overwhelming Calamity[14] -
The Day when man will remember that for which he strove,
And Hellfire will be exposed for [all] those who see -
So as for he who transgressed
And preferred the life of the world,
Then indeed, Hellfire will be [his] refuge.
But as for he who feared the position of his Lord[15] and prevented the soul from [unlawful] inclination,
Then indeed, Paradise will be [his] refuge.
They ask you, [O Muḥammad], about the Hour: when is its arrival?[16]
In what [position] are you that you should mention it?[17]
To your Lord is its finality.[18]
You are only a warner for those who fear it.
It will be, on the Day they see it,[19] as though they had not remained [in the world] except for an afternoon or a morning thereof.

footnotes.1: i.e., those who tear out the souls of those destined for Hell.
footnotes.2: i.e., those angels who ease out the souls of those destined for Paradise.
footnotes.4: Racing to deliver the souls of the believers to Paradise.
footnotes.6: Those of the disbelievers who denied the Resurrection.
footnotes.8: The disbelievers say this in ridicule of the warning.
footnotes.9: i.e., "If that were so, we would not be able to escape punishment."
footnotes.10: i.e., the miracle of his staff becoming a great snake.
footnotes.11: An alternative meaning is "running [from the snake]."
footnotes.12: i.e., for Pharaoh's setting himself up as a deity and for his previous oppression of the people and denial of Moses.
footnotes.13: i.e., created the day from within the surrounding darkness.
footnotes.17: Meaning that Muḥammad (ﷺ) had no knowledge of it, so how could he inform them?
footnotes.18: i.e., its destination and termination. And to Him belongs ultimate knowledge of it.
